title: Declare local worktree review state through MakeMe

intentCoverage.report:
Verdict: Caught (on the materializeLocalCheckout / buildRepository path).

Story and revision: SEED-353#declare-local-worktree-review-state ("Declare local worktree review state through MakeMe"), plan .planning/slice-plans/708-declare-local-worktree-review-state/PLAN.md, at 16d697ab412befcd738add2544040b3248ecc72d. I checked it in a detached scratch worktree at <job tmp>/ic-scratch. Its pre-probe state was clean (0 porcelain entries).

Promise (Key example 1): Story A's declared worktree has a staged edit, an unstaged edit, an untracked nested file and an ignored log. Git must report the declared porcelain status and the declared staged names.

Fault: Distribution/tests/support/repository-local-state.mjs, writeLocalState. I replaced the line `if (staged.length > 0) git("add", "--", ...staged);` with a comment, so the declared staged files are written but never added to the index. I kept the suggested fault. I checked reach with git grep: writeLocalState is the only place staging happens, and both materializers call it. These are Distribution/tests/support/repository-history.mjs:221 (buildRepository / materializeLocalCheckout, the path the node test uses) and dashboard/test-support/support/startOriginWorkspace.ts:72 (the start-origin path that Story A's E2E consumers use). So this one fault reaches both paths. I did not try the alternative fault, which skips staging on the start-origin path only.

Maintained check examined: Distribution/tests/support/repository-local-state.test.mjs, test "declared local state is what Git reports of the index and files". The command was `node --test Distribution/tests/support/repository-local-state.test.mjs` on Node v24.21.0.

Runs:
- Baseline: the test passed (1 pass, 0 fail, duration_ms 242.5).
- Independent witness under the fault: a scratch node test (deleted afterwards) materialized a workspace declared with staged {staged.txt, added.txt}. `git status --porcelain=v1` reported " M staged.txt" and "?? added.txt", and `git diff --cached --name-status` was empty. That is wrong behavior on the intended path: the declared staged files are not staged.
- Faulted maintained run: the test failed (0 pass, 1 fail). The failure is the first `assert.equal` at repository-local-state.test.mjs:34, the porcelain status comparison. It expected "A  added.txt" and "M  staged.txt" but got " M staged.txt" and "?? added.txt". The later `git diff --cached --name-status` assertion was not reached.
- Restoration: an EXIT trap copied back the original file. Afterwards `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --stat` were empty, matching the pre-probe state. The same command passed again (1 pass, 0 fail, duration_ms 246.0). I then removed the scratch worktree with `git worktree remove --force`; `git worktree list` no longer shows it, and the execution checkout is still clean.

Claim limit: the catch is proven only on the materializeLocalCheckout path that the node test drives. I did not run the Story A E2E review proof (e2e/review/story-review.spec.ts). This probe adds no new evidence about whether that proof can tell staged from unstaged starting state. The existing execution premise D1 already records that it cannot: removing `git add staged.txt` left 9 E2E cases green. This catch matches the planned answer in slice 2, which is the node test as the independent check. Because the start-origin path shares writeLocalState, a fault inside writeLocalState is caught. A fault that skipped staging only in startOriginWorkspace.ts, outside writeLocalState, would per D1 go uncaught by the E2E. That variant was not probed here.

Next proof action: none needed for the writeLocalState staging promise. If the caller wants start-origin-specific staging covered, the next step is to probe the start-origin-only variant against the E2E review spec.

Costs:
- Test runtime: measured, node test runner duration_ms. Baseline 242.5 ms, faulted 260.3 ms, restored 246.0 ms. The scratch witness run took about 155 ms (test-reported). No Playwright run.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part in this invocation and there is no separate measure.
- Agent effort: unavailable as a separately supported measure. My only observation is about 9 tool calls in this run, which is a count and not a measure of time or tokens.
- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 40994 ms (measured), from 1795027337403 to 1795027378397 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: 16d697ab412befcd738add2544040b3248ecc72d, Caught, no follow-up — start origins apply local state only through the shared writeLocalState call, so the checked catch covers their staging.
